key_insight: Atomically engineered LaVO3/PrVO3 superlattices enable control of structural distortions and antiferromagnetic transition temperature by varying layer proportions.
engineering_relevance: Interface and strain engineering offer a route to tunable magnetic perovskite oxides; the abstract does not report AI methods or solar-cell applications.
method: Grow layered superlattices by molecular beam epitaxy on (001) SrTiO3.
Characterize epitaxy and atomic displacements using X-ray diffraction, reciprocal space mapping, and high-resolution STEM.
Probe layer-resolved orbital hybridization and relate it to oxygen-octahedra rotations.
evidence_signal: Diffraction confirms crystalline quality and strain state, while microscopy and spectroscopy reveal periodicity-dependent displacements and hybridization; the abstract reports a tunable antiferromagnetic transition without numerical values.
watch_item: Trilinear coupling is visualized indirectly through structural and spectroscopic proxies rather than measured directly.
